The short silver trade is becoming crowded.

Silver's 3-month silver put-call skew is up to -3 points, its highest level since early July.

This metric measures the relative cost of put options to call options and is up +10 points over the last 4 weeks, signaling growing demand for bearish bets on silver prices.

Over the last 12 months, this metric has been higher only 2% of the time.

Meanwhile, speculative investors, including hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), sold -$2.2 billion in silver futures over the 3 weeks ending October 13th.

As a result, their net long positioning is down to just +$1.7 billion, the lowest in at least 2 years.

For perspective, this metric stood at +$8.5 billion in December 2025.

Investors are extremely bearish on silver.

BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 YoY, or +5%, to a record $28,303.

This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase of at least +$1,300.

Over this period, the average annual premium for family coverage has surged +$5,884, or +26%.

To put this into perspective, CPI inflation has risen +13% over the same period, or half as much.

Since 1999, the average health insurance premium for a family has soared +$22,494, or +387%.

This represents an average annual growth rate of +6.1%, well above CPI inflation at +2.6% over the same period.

Health insurance has never been more expensive.

Semiconductor prices are skyrocketing in the US:

Producer prices for semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing surged +26% YoY in September, their 4th-largest increase on record.

This also marks their 6th consecutive YoY increase of at least +25%.

Since July 2025, the Producer Price Index for semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing has risen +31%, to its 2nd-highest level since January 2007.

To put this into perspective, the index declined every year from 1994 to 2021.

Meanwhile, producer prices for electronic components and accessories soared +27% YoY last month, also marking their 6th consecutive YoY increase of at least +25%.

The AI Revolution is driving historic technology inflation.

RT @MilkRoadAI: Tom Lee thinks we are getting a lot closer to the bottom of this tech selloff than people realize.

His argument is that in…

No matter how farfetched the idea might be of the Treasury Department repricing its gold to create cashflows out of thin air, even a remote possibility that desperate governments will do desperate things is a reminder to always have real assets in the portfolio. On that note, I continue to be impressed by Bitcoin’s resilience. I think it will be eating gold’s lunch for a while, although I remain bullish on both.

Far-fetched? Of course, but these days I have learned to never be shocked by anything anymore. Notwithstanding that an action like this would require congressional approval, my guess is that if the Treasury were attempt do this, it would backfire in a big way. A trillion is only half of one year’s budget deficit, after all. The dollar would take a hit, and the term premium would rise further. 🧵(2/2)

Finally, and now for something completely different. There has been some buzz lately over what other tricks the Treasury Department might have up its sleeve to try to bring down the cost of funding. The long-dated off-the-run buybacks certainly didn’t work (other than daring the bond vigilantes to show us who is in charge). Now an old meme has re-emerged. What if the Treasury were to mark-to-market its gold reserves, which the Fed holds on its behalf? Imagine if they repriced their gold holdings from the $42/oz that has been in place since the early 1970’s to the $4,200/oz that gold is worth today? The Treasury would become an instant $1 trillion richer (hence the trillion-dollar coin meme that has floated around for a few years). 

How would that work? It seems to work as follows: The Fed would all of a sudden have an extra $1 trillion in assets (grey bar at the top right of the chart below) on its balance sheet, and the liability offset would be the Treasury’s cash account at the Fed (TGA). Voila, the Treasury would have an extra trillion to spend without having to issue more debt. 🧵(1/2)

BREAKING: AI token spending grew just +0.2% MoM in September, the lowest monthly growth since November 2025.

This follows a +1.0% increase in August, marking two consecutive months of growth at or below +1.0%, the weakest streak in at least 18 months.

This comes as falling prices for the most advanced AI models, alongside improvements in efficiency and quality, drive down the average price per million tokens processed by these models.

Since July, overall AI token prices have declined -48%, to $0.65 per million tokens, the lowest since at least January 2026.

Lower costs could unlock the next wave of AI adoption.

Descending triangle is a bearish chart pattern. Its downward sloping upper boundary gives the pattern the bearish bias. This is from 1930s Edwards & Magee. Descending triangle breakdown followed by a symmetrical triangle acting as a bearish continuation. https://t.co/s38f0cEAaG

The literature on this goes back to 1920s with Richard W. Schabacker. 

Charts are still the same. Price dynamics haven't changed.

The only difference is we can chart 1000s of them at every time frame we want. In those days each bar was plotted by hand on millimetric paper.

Right now its eyeballing technique, soon it will be AI that captures these setups.

We expect a large wave of US stock buybacks ahead.

BREAKING: The total value of the US stock market has surged to 350% of the US M2 money supply, the highest level since the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.

Since the 2022 bear market, this ratio has surged +170 percentage points.

Over this period, the S&P 500 has rallied +118%, while M2 has risen +9%.

In other words, the stock market's gain has outpaced the money supply growth by 13x.

The last time equity market growth exceeded M2 growth by a larger amount was from 1995 to 1999.

Asset owners are winning.
